newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Alestra makes first long-distance call.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Alestra makes first long-distance call.

text.p: Alestra, the telephone company formed by Grupo Industrial Alfa, Valores Industriales, Grupo Financiero Bancomer and AT&T Corp, made its first long-distance phone call in Mexico through its new fiber-optic network, the company said Thursday in a statement.
Queretaro state governor, Enrique Burgos Garcia, made the call on Wednesday to Alestra president Jorge Escalona in Monterrey, Nuevo Leon, the company said.

Mexico's long distance telephone service began its gradual opening to competition on Jan. 1 in the city of Queretaro, ending the former monopoly of Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) in the estimated $4 billion market.

An independent group contracted to tally telephone service found Alestra the top choice for callers in the city of Queretaro. The group said 55.8 percent of residents chose the company for its long distance service as of last Dec. 12, Alestra said.

The company's rates are 1.90 pesos per minute during the day and 95 centavos at night. Telmex charges 1.998 pesos per minute in the day and 0.994 pesos at night while MCI Communications Corp and Grupo Financiero Banamex Accival venture Avantel charges two pesos per minute in the day and one peso at night.
